subject: SummitHR: sustained token-starve causing 5xx spike — emergency headroom & fallbacks
messages:
From: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@summithr.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: engops@summithr.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production 5xx & prolonged latency — SummitHR dedicated pool

Rachel —

We started seeing sustained 5xx errors and large tail latency on our inference calls starting ~08:45 PDT. Error rate climbed from 0.2% to ~6.8% and p95 latency jumped from 180ms to 1.6s. This is hitting our live candidate scoring pipeline and creating processing backpressure upstream.

Attached is a lightweight CSV with sample metrics (token rates, queue depth, 5xx counts) for the past two hours. We are on a reserved dedicated pool (contract SUM-2026-1187) and our SLA requires consistent throughput for our peak window.

Immediate asks:
- Can Redwood open emergency headroom or authorize burst capacity while we investigate?
- If that’s not possible, can you enable programmatic fallback to your hosted model variant to drain the queue?
- We need ETA for a mitigation step we can present to our execs in 30 minutes.

This is customer-impacting — Alyssa (CTO) is ready to escalate if we don’t have a plan quickly.

Thanks,
Alyssa Morgan
Head of Platform, SummitHR

Attachments: summithr-token-metrics-20260829.csv

From: rachel.kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@summithr.com>

Subject: Re: Production 5xx & prolonged latency — SummitHR dedicated pool

Alyssa — thank you for the data and the heads-up. We’re on it.

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
1) Ops (David) is starting an urgent investigation into the reserved pool saturation and queueing.
2) I can request a temporary burst (headroom) authorization — that typically takes 10–20 minutes if leadership approves.
3) We’ll prepare a controlled routing fallback to our highest-compat hosted variant to reduce pressure on the dedicated pool; we need your sign-off for any change that alters model outputs.

Please keep the CSV coming; if you can also share a small sample request+response payload (anonymized), that’ll help our reproduce. I’ll coordinate the exec path if headroom is denied.

I’m moving this to priority — we’ll update every 15 minutes.

—Rachel Kim
Director, Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: david.kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: rachel.kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@summithr.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production 5xx & prolonged latency — SummitHR dedicated pool

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed: Dedicated GPU pool assigned to SUM-2026-1187 has an abrupt token-rate spike at 08:42 PDT; sustained high concurrency pushed queue depth above the pooling window.
- Impacts: KV cache pressure + scheduler backoff -> synchronous request queueing -> increased p95 and 5xx when queue hits per-worker max inflight.
- Root candidates: sudden customer token surge (confirmed by attached metrics), plus one worker instance that reported repeated OOM-retries at 08:50 (log snippets attached to internal diagnostics link).

Immediate mitigations I can execute now (require consent for fallback):
A) Authorize temporary burst on Dedicated pool + spin up 2 extra worker slots (estimated 8–12 min to be effective).
B) Programmatic fallback: re-route 25–50% of traffic to Redwood-hosted compatible model (same architecture, slightly smaller context) — near-instant cutover but will add small differences to outputs.
C) Throttle large requests from SummitHR for a 10-minute window via rate-limit override.

My recommendation: Do (B) immediately to relieve the queue while I kick off (A). We need Alyssa to confirm she’s OK with a partial hosted fallback for the next 30–60 minutes.

-David (SRE)

[internal link: diagnostics/logs/rkm/sum-1187/20260829]

We appreciate the fast response. We’re wary of any fallback that changes scoring determinism; SummitHR needs consistent candidate ranking. That said, our priority is availability.

Actions from our side:
- We can temporarily limit concurrent scoring jobs from the nightly enrichment pipeline (will reduce throughput ~40%) — we’ll flip that now.
- We’re attaching a sanitized sample payload and full request logs for 08:30–09:10.

Please confirm if Redwood will:
1) Start a 25% hosted fallback now (we accept slight output variance for a short window).
2) If Redwood requests burst capacity, we need an explicit headroom authorization and a timeline for when that will be revoked.

Thanks — EngOps Team

Subject: Re: SummitHR: sustained token-starve causing 5xx spike — emergency headroom & fallbacks

Alyssa — update and recommended plan for your execs:

What we did (09:25–11:10 PDT):
- Deployed a 25% programmatic fallback to Redwood-hosted compatible model; immediate reduction in dedicated queue depth observed.
- Spun 2 additional worker slots under emergency burst authorization (authorized by commercial) — brought headroom +18%.
- Applied a short throttle on nightly enrichment jobs (customer action) to keep steady-state.

Impact (observed):
- 5xx rate dropped from 6.8% to 0.6% within 12 minutes of fallback and burst being live.
- p95 latency reduced from 1.6s to 240ms after worker spin-up and fallback.

Next steps (owner):
- David: follow up with postmortem and root cause (expected within 24 hours).
- Priyom: run a model-compatibility verification for hosted fallback and quantify delta in scoring outputs (24–48 hours).
- Naomi + Marissa: commercial follow-up on credit and permanent capacity adjustment options.

We’ll also schedule a 30-minute after-action with SummitHR Engineering tomorrow to review permanent remediation — proposed time 11:00 PDT. Please confirm.

If you want an immediate CEO-level summary, Marissa can join the 10:30 sync. Thanks for patience and quick coordination; we consider this resolved for now but are keeping an elevated watch for two more hours.

—Rachel Kim
Director, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
